title: Naturality of the scalar-extension regular-module comparison
statement: Let C be a braided monoidal category with coequalizers preserved by tensoring on either side, let R be a commutative monoid object, let S be a monoid object, and let φ:R→S be a monoid homomorphism. Extension of scalars sends the regular R-module canonically to the regular S-module. If regular endomorphisms p of R and q of S satisfy p.hom≫φ=φ≫q.hom, the scalar-extended p is intertwined with q by this regular-module isomorphism.

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: View φ as an R-linear map from regular R to the restriction of regular S; linearity is precisely multiplicativity of φ. Its adjoint f is a map from the scalar extension of regular R to regular S.

Construct g in the reverse direction as the unique S-linear regular lift of the image of 1 under the adjunction unit. The identity g f=id follows by evaluation on 1 and preservation of the unit by φ. For f g=id, apply the extension-restriction Hom equivalence and then regular-module extensionality on 1. This produces the isomorphism using actual maps, without any existence choice.

For naturality, apply the same Hom equivalence. Naturality of the extension unit, computed from its tensor-coequalizer formula, moves the extended p past the unit. The extension Hom beta identity reduces the resulting equation exactly to p.hom≫φ=φ≫q.hom.

lean.statement:
theorem regularExtensionIso_naturality
    (p : regular R ⟶ regular R) (q : regular S ⟶ regular S)
    (h : p.hom ≫ φ = φ ≫ q.hom) :
    (extendScalars φ).map p ≫ (regularExtensionIso φ).hom =
      (regularExtensionIso φ).hom ≫ q
